requirements.statement: The web application SHALL route the primary Desk to / and SHALL redirect the /desk alias and demoted feature paths into that Desk shell.
requirements.rationale: The Desk is the product shell and route ownership must be observable.

sources.claim: / is the primary Desk route and /welcome and /presence are the other real product routes.
/desk and unknown paths redirect to /.

requirements.acceptance: Opening / mounts DeskApp; /desk and unknown paths reach /; demoted paths stage their surface and return to the shell.
requirements.test: Actual: web/src/routes.test.ts asserts product routes and demoted-route declarations; App routing behavior is source-inspected.
requirements.gap: No product-level route telemetry is recorded.

requirements.statement: The Desk SHOULD keep spatial objects and the list view projections of the same object records consistent.
requirements.rationale: The user needs to move between a Workbench view and inspectable rows without losing identity.

sources.claim: World descriptors carry stable ids, kinds, labels and positions.
DeskApp mounts world floor, list, windows and chrome from the same Desk surface.

requirements.acceptance: A selected object has the same id and label in world and list projections.
requirements.test: Proposed: add a projection parity assertion for every WORLD_OBJECTS descriptor.
requirements.gap: No current assertion compares all projections.

requirements.statement: The Desk SHALL represent each world object with a stable kind, id, label, subtitle, position, visual metadata and available verbs.
requirements.rationale: Portable object records are the source of truth for rendering, menu availability and persistence.

sources.claim: Primitive descriptors define the object kind and display/source fields.
World objects define id, kind, label, subtitle, position, tint, texture and verbs.

requirements.acceptance: A descriptor can render in a world or list projection without inferred fields.
requirements.test: Actual: web/src/desk/__tests__/desk.test.ts asserts canonical world ordering, filtering, deterministic placement and clamping.
requirements.gap: The descriptor type does not yet carry a persisted selection or receipt field.

requirements.statement: The Desk SHALL communicate selection and state with geometry, labels or marks in addition to colour.
requirements.rationale: A selected or waiting object must remain legible to colour-blind users and in reduced visual modes.

sources.claim: Selection is a geometry/state treatment and never colour alone.
World descriptors provide labels and state-facing visual fields.

requirements.acceptance: Selected, unavailable and pending records expose text or shape cues in snapshots.
requirements.test: Proposed: accessibility snapshot checks selected, unavailable and pending states without colour inspection.
requirements.gap: The Pixi object state parity is not exhaustively asserted.

requirements.statement: Every actionable Desk object SHOULD have pointer, touch and keyboard ways to open its inspection surface.
requirements.rationale: A spatial canvas cannot be the only access path for the first user or assistive technology.

sources.claim: Object activation has an equivalent list or keyboard path.
DeskApp mounts the list projection alongside the world.

requirements.acceptance: The list projection opens the same object as a world click and a keyboard activation.
requirements.test: Proposed: Playwright or RTL parity test for pointer, touch and Enter activation.
requirements.gap: Touch-specific activation is not separately covered.

requirements.statement: A Desk window SHALL use the shared frame contract for title, focus, close, minimize, maximize, move and resize.
requirements.rationale: Window verbs must feel like one Workbench system across all surfaces.

sources.claim: DeskWindow composes the shared window frame and content slots.
The frame owns focus, chrome and geometry callbacks.

requirements.acceptance: Every registered window renders the same frame controls and focus treatment.
requirements.test: Actual: web/src/desk/__tests__/windows.test.tsx asserts frame controls and window lifecycle behavior.
requirements.gap: There is no catalogue assertion that every registry entry uses DeskWindowFrame.

requirements.statement: The Desk SHALL persist window order, panel geometry, open windows, zone placement and relevant preferences under a versioned workspace key.
requirements.rationale: A workbench is useful when it restores the operator's arrangement without serializing transient runtime state.

sources.claim: Workspace persistence uses hs.desk.workspace.v1 and an explicit version.
The saved shape contains panel rectangle/order, windowsById, zoneWindows and prefs.

requirements.acceptance: Reload restores the saved arrangement and rejects a wrong version without throwing.
requirements.test: Actual: web/src/desk/__tests__/windows.test.tsx asserts the v1 round-trip, reset removal and lifecycle persistence.
requirements.gap: No migration registry exists for a future v2 shape.

requirements.statement: Closing or focusing a Desk window SHALL return focus to a deterministic surviving target.
requirements.rationale: Focus loss makes the Workbench unusable for keyboard and screen-reader operators.

sources.claim: Window focus is assigned through the desk focus store and active id.

sources.symbol: exactly the front window wears is-front; raising moves it
sources.claim: The test asserts is-front follows the raised window. Other lifecycle tests cover close callbacks and minimized depth; opener focus return is not proved here.

requirements.acceptance: After close, focus lands on the next registered window or the Desk focus target.
requirements.test: Actual: web/src/desk/__tests__/windows.test.tsx asserts the active and closed window states.
requirements.gap: Focus restoration across a browser reload is not tested.

requirements.statement: Window movement and resize SHALL clamp to the available work rectangle and preserve minimum dimensions.
requirements.rationale: The owner must always be able to recover a window and its controls.

sources.claim: Geometry constants define work margins, minimums and snap thresholds.
Rectangles are clamped to work bounds while respecting minimum dimensions.

requirements.acceptance: A drag or resize beyond every edge produces a rect inside work bounds with minW/minH.
requirements.test: Actual: web/src/desk/__tests__/shell.test.tsx asserts snap, placement, resize, Expose and clamp numerical boundaries.
requirements.gap: The algorithm is single-viewport; native multi-monitor work areas are outside the web contract.

requirements.statement: A future native host MAY persist and restore per-display work areas without changing the web workspace schema.
requirements.rationale: Desktop displays can have separate coordinate spaces and device scale factors.

sources.claim: The proposed native seam owns host capabilities and display-aware integration.
The current web schema has one viewport work rectangle.

requirements.acceptance: A host adapter can supply a display work area while web persistence remains backward compatible.
requirements.test: Proposed: host contract test with two display work areas and a web-schema round trip.
requirements.gap: No native host is installed or declared in this repository.

requirements.statement: The Desk SHALL maintain one current context and route primary keyboard verbs through that context.
requirements.rationale: A single context prevents a canvas click, row focus and window focus from invoking different records.

sources.claim: The Desk keymap binds one document handler and reads current context.
Desk stores own selection and active window state.

requirements.acceptance: The active object and active window are the same context used by menu and shortcut actions.
requirements.test: Actual: web/src/desk/__tests__/keymap.test.ts asserts the current context is used for primary actions.
requirements.gap: Cross-window selection history is not persisted.

requirements.statement: The Desk SHOULD support range, marquee and select-all semantics with a stable ordering rule.
requirements.rationale: Batch work is required for a Workbench with many objects and should not depend on repeated single clicks.

sources.claim: The brief calls for selection, focus and keyboard behavior as explicit SRS concerns.
Current keymap covers single-context verbs but has no range or marquee command.

requirements.acceptance: Shift selection, marquee selection and a named select-all verb produce deterministic id order.
requirements.test: Proposed: interaction tests for range, marquee and select-all with keyboard and pointer inputs.
requirements.gap: No current selection model or implementation for these gestures.

requirements.statement: The Desk SHALL derive context menu rows from the verb registry and expose a stable id, label, enabled state and runner for each row.
requirements.rationale: One registry prevents menus, keyboard shortcuts and command surfaces from drifting.

sources.claim: Verb definitions include id, label, availability and run behavior.
The Desk verb registry is the source of menu actions.

requirements.acceptance: A registered verb renders once in a menu with its availability and executes its runner.
requirements.test: Actual: web/src/desk/__tests__/verbRegistry.test.ts asserts registry ids, labels, availability and runner calls.
requirements.gap: The registry has no generated machine-readable catalogue artifact.

requirements.statement: Unavailable verbs SHALL remain inspectable with an explicit reason and SHALL not run.
requirements.rationale: Ghost actions explain the next possible move without pretending that a blocked operation succeeded.

sources.claim: Verb availability carries a reason and disabled state.

sources.symbol: object verbs ghost WITH a reason when nothing is selected
sources.claim: The test asserts unselected object verbs carry ghost reasons; keyboard dispatch refusal is covered separately in keymap.test.ts.

requirements.acceptance: A blocked row displays its reason and its runner is not called.
requirements.test: Actual: web/src/desk/__tests__/verbRegistry.test.ts asserts ghost reason and no runner invocation.
requirements.gap: Reason strings are not yet localized.

requirements.statement: A verb SHALL resolve execution in its owning interaction context; a metadata-only registry runner must not be treated as proof that the feature is unavailable.
requirements.rationale: Thread slash IDs share command vocabulary while the composer and pullout own the actual handlers.

sources.claim: The registry comment assigns slash triggers to the composer and handlers to the pullout.
The switch invokes keep/fork/stop/new callbacks and typed todo/compact requests.

requirements.acceptance: Keep, fork, stop and other slash commands reach their composer callbacks or typed API paths; generic menu availability respects the owning context.
requirements.test: Source: ThreadComposer.executeSlashCommand dispatches callbacks and typed API requests. Existing registry tests check slash-ID parity; a complete callback execution matrix was not inspected.
requirements.gap: Document and test the executor ownership contract across every command adapter; do not disable functional Thread commands merely because registry run is empty.

requirements.statement: Desk keyboard handling SHALL use one guarded binder, reserve platform modifiers, and ignore shortcuts while typing in editable controls.
requirements.rationale: Keyboard behavior must be predictable and must not corrupt text entry.

sources.claim: The keymap uses one document listener, typing guards and primary meta-or-control matching.

sources.symbol: ⌘ means the primary modifier (meta OR ctrl, never both)
sources.claim: The test asserts primary modifier matching for meta or ctrl and rejection of both. Dispatch tests separately assert registry actions.

requirements.acceptance: Typing in input, textarea or contenteditable does not invoke Desk verbs; the same primary key works on platform modifier.
requirements.test: Actual: web/src/desk/__tests__/keymap.test.ts asserts typing guard and primary shortcut behavior.
requirements.gap: The current map has no locale-aware shortcut label registry.

requirements.statement: Desk shortcuts SHOULD avoid browser, screen-reader and operating-system conflicts and expose their alternate label.
requirements.rationale: A shortcut that conflicts with the host cannot be a dependable product verb.

sources.claim: parseKey reads registry chord strings; it has no host-specific reserved-shortcut conflict metadata.

requirements.acceptance: Each shortcut has a conflict review and an alternate command path.
requirements.test: Proposed: static shortcut conflict matrix plus browser-level keyboard assertions.
requirements.gap: No conflict matrix or localized shortcut metadata is present.

requirements.statement: Internal drag and drop SHALL use an explicit source-kind to target-kind matrix and reject unlisted pairs.
requirements.rationale: Drop effects are domain operations and must not be inferred from a generic browser drop.

sources.claim: The drop matrix enumerates supported source and target kinds.

sources.symbol: unlisted pairs refuse (inert, never a guess)
sources.claim: Tests assert allowed pairs and null for unlisted pairs.

requirements.acceptance: An allowed pair yields a named effect; any unlisted pair yields no operation.
requirements.test: Actual: web/src/desk/__tests__/dropMatrix.test.ts asserts allowed effects and rejected pairs.
requirements.gap: The matrix is not yet shared with native file-drop adapters.

requirements.statement: Every supported drag operation SHALL have an equivalent keyboard or menu action.
requirements.rationale: Dragging is a pointer convenience and cannot be the only route to a domain operation.

sources.claim: The current matrix describes drag effects only.
Verbs are the available non-drag command surface.

requirements.acceptance: For each matrix effect, a named verb is available from the source or target context.
requirements.test: Proposed: matrix-to-verb coverage test requiring one registry id per effect.
requirements.gap: Some internal drop effects have no documented non-drag command.

requirements.statement: A supported external file drop SHALL show a named release target and route the file to the importer; a hold action SHALL show its run target.
requirements.rationale: Egress and destructive or consequential actions need visible destination feedback.

sources.claim: External file drops are accepted only over a registered release target.
Allowed drops carry named effects such as Hold or Add to Knowledge.

requirements.acceptance: Dragover names the target and drop dispatches the importer/effect exactly once.
requirements.test: Actual: web/src/desk/__tests__/dropMatrix.test.ts asserts effect naming; GlassDropLayer tests assert external drop dispatch.
requirements.gap: The external file importer has no full error receipt in the Desk surface.

requirements.statement: The Desk SHOULD define multi-select, cross-window and orb drag semantics before exposing them in the face.
requirements.rationale: Ambiguous transfer semantics create silent duplication or loss.

sources.claim: The brief requires drag/drop exceptions and recovery to be specified.
The current matrix has no multi-select, cross-window or orb entries.

requirements.acceptance: Each new drag class has a source, target, effect, cancellation and receipt rule before implementation.
requirements.test: Proposed: scenario matrix review with executable interaction tests after design settlement.
requirements.gap: No current contract for these drag classes.

requirements.statement: An object inspection surface SHALL expose identity, current state, source/provenance and available verbs through the shared surface contract.
requirements.rationale: The operator needs to know what an object is, where it came from and what can happen next.

sources.claim: The surface contract defines identity, state, provenance and verbs as the shared content grammar.
Shared surface components are exported through one barrel.

requirements.acceptance: A registered window can render these sections without bespoke frame markup.
requirements.test: Actual: web/src/desk/__tests__/shell.test.tsx asserts shared surface identity and verb rendering in a window.
requirements.gap: Not every existing window has a provenance row.

requirements.statement: A completed domain verb SHOULD produce a durable receipt with status, egress boundary, timestamp and inspectable source.
requirements.rationale: An operator must distinguish accepted, running, failed and completed work after focus moves.

sources.claim: Receipt currently renders status, label and optional timestamp.
Verb runners currently return local actions rather than a unified receipt record.

requirements.acceptance: Every async verb writes one receipt row that survives window close and has an inspect action.
requirements.test: Proposed: verb-to-receipt integration test covering accepted, failed, retried and offline outcomes.
requirements.gap: The current Receipt component is presentational and not a persistence contract.

requirements.statement: Runtime-backed surfaces SHALL distinguish connecting, connected, reconnecting and offline states and SHALL not display offline data as current.
requirements.rationale: Truthful freshness is part of the product contract.

sources.claim: RuntimeBus exposes connecting, connected, reconnecting and offline states.
Malformed frames are ignored and reconnection is bounded.

requirements.acceptance: The chrome and affected surfaces show the current runtime state and preserve last-known data as stale.
requirements.test: Actual: web/src/runtime/RuntimeBus.test.tsx asserts one socket, connection state and delivered frame behavior.
requirements.gap: Not every Desk window subscribes to freshness state.

requirements.statement: After reconnection, affected surfaces SHOULD refetch or reconcile their stale records and expose an outcome.
requirements.rationale: Reconnecting a socket does not make records current by itself.

sources.claim: The bus reconnects the transport but does not own domain refetch.
Domain requests are separate from the runtime bus.

requirements.acceptance: A reconnect event causes each subscribed surface to reconcile and records success or failure.
requirements.test: Proposed: reconnect integration test with stale record, successful refetch and failed refetch receipt.
requirements.gap: The current bus has no common subscriber/refetch protocol.

requirements.statement: A future native DesktopHost SHALL expose only typed capabilities required by the Desk and SHALL keep permissions explicit.
requirements.rationale: Native integration must not turn a web surface into an ambient filesystem or process authority.

sources.claim: The proposed host seam bounds desktop capabilities behind explicit interfaces.
The current product is a web application with browser APIs as its runtime boundary.

requirements.acceptance: Host calls pass schema validation and deny capabilities not declared by the adapter.
requirements.test: Proposed: contract tests for capability allowlist, invalid arguments and denied permission.
requirements.gap: No native host implementation is installed or declared.

requirements.statement: The web Desk SHALL remain usable when no native host is available.
requirements.rationale: Browser delivery is the current product runtime and must remain a complete baseline.

sources.claim: The application mounts through the browser entry point.
Native hosting is a proposed integration seam, not a current dependency.

requirements.acceptance: No host object is required to load /desk, inspect local objects and use web-supported verbs.
requirements.test: Actual: web/src/routes.test.tsx and web/src/desk/__tests__/shell.test.tsx exercise the browser path without a host adapter.
requirements.gap: The fallback boundary is not documented in a runtime capability manifest.

requirements.statement: Desk actions SHALL be reachable by keyboard with visible focus and semantic names.
requirements.rationale: Keyboard access is a core path for a dense desktop surface.

sources.claim: Desk shortcuts and typing guards are implemented.
Transport keys render native buttons with aria labels and pressed state.

requirements.acceptance: All interactive catalogue components have a semantic name, visible focus and keyboard activation.
requirements.test: Actual: web/src/desk/__tests__/keymap.test.ts and component assertions cover current keyboard paths; Proposed: axe scan for the complete catalogue.
requirements.gap: The full Desk route lacks a maintained WCAG assertion suite.

requirements.statement: The Desk SHALL keep the focused control at least not entirely hidden by windows, menus or the virtual keyboard; the product target SHOULD keep it fully visible.
requirements.rationale: WCAG focus visibility and the product's dense window model require focus recovery after movement and resize.

sources.claim: The research records the focus-not-obscured baseline and stronger full-visibility target.
The current frame manages focus target selection but not viewport reveal.

requirements.acceptance: Moving/resizing a window or opening a menu never leaves the active control entirely hidden and returns it into view where possible.
requirements.test: Proposed: browser focus-obscuration scenarios at 1440 and 393 viewport sizes.
requirements.gap: No scroll/reveal or overlap assertion exists.

requirements.statement: Every drag operation SHALL have both a keyboard-accessible path and a simple non-drag pointer path with equivalent result and feedback.
requirements.rationale: Pointer drag is not an accessible interaction by itself.

sources.claim: The current interaction matrix only defines drag pairs.
Product actions must remain operable through named verbs and keyboard paths.

requirements.acceptance: Complete each supported drop effect by keyboard and separately by simple click/tap without dragging; both use the same semantic command and outcome.
requirements.test: Proposed: keyboard-only scenario tests for every DROP_MATRIX effect.
requirements.gap: Drop-to-verb coverage is not implemented.

requirements.statement: Desk surfaces SHOULD reflow at compact widths without losing an action, state, source or egress indicator.
requirements.rationale: The same object model must remain usable on narrow browser windows and touch devices.

sources.claim: Surface columns stack through surface CSS container rules.
The proposed compact target retains identity, state, action and egress information.

requirements.acceptance: At 393px, identity, state, primary verb and egress badge remain reachable without horizontal clipping.
requirements.test: Proposed: visual and semantic assertions at 393px for each window family.
requirements.gap: No complete compact viewport evidence exists.

requirements.statement: State, selection, focus and egress SHALL have non-colour cues.
requirements.rationale: Meaning must survive colour vision deficiency, forced colours and monochrome output.

sources.claim: Meters expose labels and ARIA values alongside segments.
Lamp labels are rendered beside the visual indicator.

requirements.acceptance: State labels or symbols remain in the DOM when colour tokens are removed.
requirements.test: Actual: component source and focused tests assert labels/ARIA; Proposed: forced-colours snapshot for all state chips.
requirements.gap: A whole-Desk forced-colours run is still needed.

requirements.statement: The spatial canvas SHALL have a semantic list or table parity view with equivalent names, states and actions.
requirements.rationale: Canvas pixels are not a reliable semantic representation for assistive technology.

sources.claim: DeskApp mounts a list surface alongside the world surface.
Rows render semantic list items and optional open buttons.

requirements.acceptance: Every world object appears in a named semantic row with the same available verbs.
requirements.test: Proposed: object census parity assertion between world descriptors and list rows.
requirements.gap: The parity test is not currently present.

requirements.statement: The Desk SHOULD keep interactive pointer and keyboard response within one 60 Hz frame under the documented object scale.
requirements.rationale: Workbench manipulation must feel direct while windows and world objects are visible together.

sources.claim: The brief requires performance budgets and runtime measurement.
DeskApp composes the world, windows, list and overlays in one runtime.

requirements.acceptance: Pointer move, drag and shortcut actions meet the recorded frame budget at the supported object count.
requirements.test: Proposed: Playwright performance trace with 60 Hz frame and long-task assertions at 1440px.
requirements.gap: No baseline object count or trace exists.

requirements.statement: Window motion SHALL update compositor-friendly transforms and SHALL avoid full object-tree recomputation per pointer move where the current implementation permits.
requirements.rationale: The geometry loop is the most frequent Desk interaction.

sources.claim: Window drag updates a positioned frame using geometry callbacks.
Geometry calculations are pure and bounded.

requirements.acceptance: A drag trace shows transform/position updates without a long task for ordinary window counts.
requirements.test: Proposed: browser performance trace around drag with long-task threshold and render count assertion.
requirements.gap: No automated frame-budget assertion is maintained.

requirements.statement: The Desk SHOULD expose a measured first usable paint budget and lazy-load optional terminal/editor code.
requirements.rationale: Core Workbench interaction should not wait for optional heavy surfaces.

sources.claim: The terminal pane is lazy-loaded behind Suspense.
The brief requests startup and runtime performance contracts.

requirements.acceptance: The production build reports a first usable Desk mark and optional chunks are absent from the initial critical path.
requirements.test: Proposed: Lighthouse or Playwright trace with a named first-usable mark and bundle assertion.
requirements.gap: No measured budget or mark is recorded in the current docs.

requirements.statement: The Desk SHOULD document object, window and event-count limits with a degradation behavior.
requirements.rationale: An explicit ceiling prevents a dense desktop from failing silently at scale.

sources.claim: The current world has a finite descriptor list but no scale contract.
The runtime bus bounds reconnect delay but not event volume.

requirements.acceptance: At the documented ceiling the Desk remains usable; above it the surface reports a named degraded state.
requirements.test: Proposed: load test with object/window/event ceilings and a degraded-mode assertion.
requirements.gap: No capacity budget or degraded mode exists.

requirements.statement: Runtime bus reconnect SHALL use bounded backoff, a single socket and truthful connection states.
requirements.rationale: Repeated sockets and unbounded retries can duplicate events or hide a dead backend.

sources.claim: The bus owns one socket, connection states, ping cadence and bounded reconnect.
Backoff is capped and malformed frames are ignored.

requirements.acceptance: A disconnect produces one reconnect loop with a capped delay and a truthful connection state; disposal stops further attempts. No retry-exhaustion behavior is inferred.
requirements.test: Actual: web/src/runtime/RuntimeBus.test.tsx asserts one socket and connection state transitions.
requirements.gap: The reconnect policy is not surfaced as a user-configurable setting.

requirements.statement: Corrupt or incompatible workspace data SHALL be ignored safely and SHALL leave a usable default Desk.
requirements.rationale: A bad local record must not strand the operator in a blank or crashed Workbench.

sources.claim: Invalid JSON, wrong version and invalid shape return an empty workspace.

requirements.acceptance: Loading corrupt data yields defaults, no exception escapes, and the next save writes the current schema.
requirements.test: Actual: web/src/desk/__tests__/windows.test.tsx asserts invalid/retired persisted slots are safely cut and reset to defaults.
requirements.gap: The recovery does not explain the discarded record to the user.

requirements.statement: Failed API, host and runtime operations SHALL preserve the last safe state and expose a named recovery action.
requirements.rationale: Recovery should retain work and explain the next safe step.

sources.claim: API errors preserve status and payload message.
SurfaceState renders error and an optional Try again action.

requirements.acceptance: A failed load keeps last-known data where safe and provides retry or export/park action.
requirements.test: Actual: component tests assert SurfaceState error/retry rendering; Proposed: API failure integration test for last-known data.
requirements.gap: Host failures and domain receipts do not share a recovery contract.

requirements.statement: All user-facing Desk labels, states, errors, menu reasons and accessible names SHALL come from a locale message catalogue.
requirements.rationale: Hard-coded English prevents reliable localization and produces inconsistent terminology.

sources.claim: Shared surfaces currently contain literal loading, error, retry and empty labels.
Verb labels and reasons are currently defined as source literals.

requirements.acceptance: A locale switch changes every catalogue label without changing domain ids.
requirements.test: Proposed: static extraction check plus locale snapshot for route, menu, state and error strings.
requirements.gap: No locale catalogue or extraction pipeline is present.

requirements.statement: Desk layout SHALL tolerate at least 30 percent expansion in compact labels and 50 percent expansion in verbose labels.
requirements.rationale: Translated labels must not clip actions or hide state.

sources.claim: Surface layout responds to its container but does not define text-expansion budgets.
The proposed design calls for localized, compact-safe surface layouts.

requirements.acceptance: Expanded pseudo-localized labels remain readable and actionable at 393px and 1440px.
requirements.test: Proposed: pseudo-localization visual/semantic run with 30/50 percent expansion fixtures.
requirements.gap: No expansion fixtures or width budget are maintained.

requirements.statement: Dates, times, numbers and byte/count values SHALL use locale-aware formatters while domain values remain canonical.
requirements.rationale: Localized presentation must not alter sorting, ids or persistence.

sources.claim: Current formatting helpers provide fixed human-readable values.
Persistence stores canonical numeric and timestamp values.

requirements.acceptance: Changing locale changes display formatting and leaves saved records byte-for-byte canonical.
requirements.test: Proposed: locale formatter tests for date/time/number and persistence invariance.
requirements.gap: Format helpers do not accept locale or Intl options.

requirements.statement: The Desk SHOULD support right-to-left layout and bidi-safe identifiers without changing object order or keyboard semantics.
requirements.rationale: Direction changes must not corrupt source labels, paths or spatial actions.

sources.claim: Identity currently renders labels without direction metadata.
The brief requires localization and accessibility themes in the SRS.

requirements.acceptance: An RTL fixture preserves readable mixed-direction labels and equivalent arrow/shortcut actions.
requirements.test: Proposed: RTL visual and keyboard fixture with mixed Latin/path content.
requirements.gap: No RTL styles or tests are present.

requirements.statement: Desk surfaces SHALL consume semantic theme tokens for material, text, state, focus and egress treatments.
requirements.rationale: A shared token graph keeps the Workbench coherent and makes contrast review possible.

sources.claim: Semantic color and surface variables are defined centrally.
Generated tokens expose the typed token set.

requirements.acceptance: A surface does not introduce an unregistered colour for a state or material role.
requirements.test: Actual: web/src/desk/__tests__/styles.test.ts asserts no forbidden ad-hoc surface colour literals.
requirements.gap: Not every legacy Desk overlay uses semantic variables.

requirements.statement: The Desk SHOULD provide a high-contrast theme that preserves state, focus, selection and egress distinctions.
requirements.rationale: Contrast and forced-colour users need a first-class Workbench treatment.

sources.claim: The current token file defines the baseline theme but no high-contrast mode.
High contrast is a proposed theme requirement.

requirements.acceptance: High-contrast snapshots retain all semantic distinctions and meet the adopted contrast target.
requirements.test: Proposed: forced-colours/high-contrast browser snapshots with axe contrast assertions.
requirements.gap: No high-contrast token layer exists.

requirements.statement: The Desk SHOULD provide light and system-selected themes using the same semantic roles.
requirements.rationale: Theme choice must not fork object, verb or state semantics.

sources.claim: The current baseline is dark-first and does not expose a complete light/system contract.

requirements.acceptance: Light and system modes render all catalogue components with equivalent state cues.
requirements.test: Proposed: theme matrix snapshots for system dark, system light and explicit light.
requirements.gap: No complete light/system theme is present.

requirements.statement: API failures SHALL preserve HTTP status and server payload where safe and SHALL map to a user-facing recovery state.
requirements.rationale: Debuggable errors and safe recovery require the original failure boundary.

sources.claim: ApiError stores status and payload message.
SurfaceState renders an error and optional retry.

requirements.acceptance: A non-2xx response retains status for logs and renders a named retry/park action.
requirements.test: Actual: web/src/lib/api.test.ts asserts ApiError status/message; Proposed: SurfaceState test asserts recovery action.
requirements.gap: There is no common error code catalogue.

requirements.statement: A rejected verb or drop SHALL explain the refusal in the same surface that offered the action.
requirements.rationale: Silent refusal leaves the operator unable to correct the action.

sources.claim: Unavailable verbs expose a reason.
Unsupported drop pairs return null.

requirements.acceptance: A rejected action leaves a named reason or refusal receipt and does not mutate the target.
requirements.test: Actual: verbRegistry and dropMatrix tests assert no runner/effect for rejected operations; Proposed: UI refusal receipt assertion.
requirements.gap: Unsupported drop UI feedback is not asserted end-to-end.

requirements.statement: Workspace save failure SHALL preserve the in-memory arrangement and expose retry without clearing the operator's desk.
requirements.rationale: A local persistence fault must not destroy current work.

sources.claim: Workspace save serializes a bounded shape but has no shared failure surface.

requirements.acceptance: A storage exception leaves in-memory state unchanged and exposes a retry or export path.
requirements.test: Proposed: mock localStorage failure and assert store state plus recovery action.
requirements.gap: Write failures are not surfaced through a user-facing receipt.

requirements.statement: Repository quality checks SHALL guard product text, token usage, surface imports and other documented Desk invariants.
requirements.rationale: The design system depends on static rules that are easy to regress in a large surface.

sources.claim: The repository has a documentation and invariant checker.

sources.symbol: computeScrollHint is not defined outside desk/surface (re-exports allowed)
sources.claim: A focused test scans source for unsupported scroll helper exports.
